title: Amazon SDE Online Assessment Mock 1
description: Simulates Amazon SDE-1 Online Assessment: Debugging & Work Simulation (20Q/35min), CS Fundamentals (20Q/35min), Logical Reasoning (15Q/25min). Total: 55 questions, 95 minutes. (Coding problems excluded — use LeetCode for coding practice.)

questions.text: Which data structure is best suited for implementing a LRU (Least Recently Used) Cache?
questions.explanation: LRU Cache uses a HashMap for O(1) lookup and a Doubly Linked List for O(1) insertion/deletion to maintain usage order.

questions.text: What is the time complexity to search an element in a balanced BST?
questions.explanation: In a balanced BST, each comparison halves the search space → O(log n).

questions.text: In Java, what is the difference between '==' and '.equals()' for String comparison?
questions.explanation: '==' checks reference equality (same object in memory). '.equals()' checks content equality.

questions.text: What does SOLID stand for in software design?
questions.explanation: SOLID: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion.

questions.text: Which algorithm finds the shortest path in a weighted graph with non-negative edges?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths in graphs with non-negative edge weights.

questions.text: What is a hash collision?
options: When two different keys produce the same hash value
When a key is not found
questions.explanation: A collision occurs when two distinct inputs produce the same hash output.

questions.text: In a linked list, what is the time complexity of accessing the nth element?
questions.explanation: Unlike arrays, linked lists don't support random access — you must traverse from head: O(n).

questions.text: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
options: Threads have more memory than processes
Threads share process memory space; processes have separate memory
questions.explanation: Threads within a process share memory/resources; processes are independent with separate memory.

questions.text: What does the 'volatile' keyword do in Java?
options: Ensures variable is read from/written to main memory, not CPU cache
questions.explanation: 'volatile' ensures all threads see the latest value from main memory, not a cached copy.

questions.text: In REST API design, which status code means 'Resource Created Successfully'?
questions.explanation: HTTP 201 Created is returned when a POST request successfully creates a new resource.

questions.text: What is memoization?
options: Caching results of expensive function calls for reuse
questions.explanation: Memoization stores results of expensive function calls and returns cached result when same inputs occur again — used in dynamic programming.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of a good hash function?
questions.explanation: A good hash function should NOT be reversible (one-way). It should be deterministic, fast, and produce uniform distribution.

questions.text: What happens when a HashMap in Java reaches its load factor threshold?
options: It rehashes and doubles its capacity
questions.explanation: When load factor is exceeded, HashMap resizes (doubles capacity) and rehashes all entries.

questions.text: In OOP, what is method overriding?
options: Defining methods with the same name but different parameters
Providing a new implementation for a parent class method in a subclass
questions.explanation: Overriding provides a specific implementation in a subclass for a method already defined in its superclass.

questions.text: What is the space complexity of DFS on a graph with V vertices and E edges?
questions.explanation: DFS uses a recursion stack of depth proportional to V (number of vertices). Space = O(V).

questions.text: What is database indexing?
options: A data structure that improves speed of data retrieval operations
questions.explanation: An index is a data structure that enables fast lookup of rows in a database table without scanning every row.

questions.text: Which design pattern ensures only one instance of a class exists?
questions.explanation: Singleton pattern restricts instantiation to a single object.

questions.text: What is tail recursion?
options: Recursion where the first call is recursive
Recursion where the recursive call is the last operation
questions.explanation: Tail recursion occurs when the recursive call is the final operation — can be optimized by compiler to avoid stack overflow.

questions.text: Which HTTP method is NOT idempotent?
questions.explanation: POST is not idempotent — calling it multiple times creates multiple resources. GET, PUT, DELETE are idempotent.

questions.text: What is the output of: List<Integer> list = new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList(1,2,3)); list.remove(Integer.valueOf(2)); System.out.println(list);
questions.explanation: Integer.valueOf(2) removes by value (not index), so 2 is removed. Result: [1, 3].

questions.text: What bug exists in: public int divide(int a, int b) { return a / b; }
questions.explanation: If b=0, this throws ArithmeticException. Should check: if(b==0) throw new IllegalArgumentException.

questions.text: What is the output? String s = null; System.out.println(s.length());
questions.explanation: Calling .length() on a null reference throws NullPointerException at runtime.

questions.text: Find the bug: for(int i=0; i<=arr.length; i++) { System.out.println(arr[i]); }
questions.explanation: Array indices go 0 to arr.length-1. Using i<=arr.length accesses arr[arr.length] which throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

questions.text: What is wrong? HashMap<String,Integer> map = new HashMap<>(); map.put('key', 1); int val = map.get('missing');
questions.explanation: map.get('missing') returns null. Unboxing null to int throws NullPointerException.

questions.text: Which code correctly swaps two integers without a temp variable?
options: a = a+b; b = a-b; a = a-b;
a = a*b; b = a/b; a = a/b;
a = a^b; b = a^b; a = a^b;
questions.explanation: All three methods (addition, multiplication, XOR) can swap two integers without a temporary variable, each with different edge cases.

questions.text: What is the issue with this recursive function? int f(int n) { return n + f(n-1); }
options: No base case — infinite recursion / StackOverflow
questions.explanation: No base case means infinite recursion → StackOverflowError.

questions.text: What does 'git rebase' do compared to 'git merge'?
options: Rewrites commit history for a linear history
questions.explanation: Rebase replays commits on top of another base, creating a linear history. Merge creates a merge commit preserving both histories.

questions.text: What is the problem with: List<String> list = new ArrayList<>(); for(String s : list) { list.remove(s); }
questions.explanation: Modifying a collection while iterating over it with enhanced for-loop throws ConcurrentModificationException.

questions.text: Which of these correctly creates a thread-safe Singleton in Java?
questions.explanation: All three approaches create thread-safe singletons. Enum Singleton is the most elegant as it handles thread-safety automatically.

questions.text: What causes a memory leak in Java?
options: Holding references to objects that are no longer needed
questions.explanation: Java's GC cannot collect objects that still have references, even if those objects are no longer logically needed (e.g., listeners, static collections).

questions.text: What is the output? int[] a = {1,2,3}; int[] b = a; b[0] = 99; System.out.println(a[0]);
questions.explanation: Arrays in Java are objects. b=a copies the reference, not the array. Modifying b[0] modifies a[0] too.

questions.text: What is wrong with this SQL? SELECT name, MAX(salary) FROM employees;
questions.explanation: Mixing aggregate (MAX) with non-aggregate (name) without GROUP BY violates SQL standard.

questions.text: The best approach to avoid SQL injection:
questions.explanation: Prepared statements prevent SQL injection by separating SQL code from user data.

questions.text: What is Big-O notation used for?
options: Describing algorithm efficiency in terms of input size
questions.explanation: Big-O notation describes how runtime or space scales with increasing input size n.

questions.text: Which is the most efficient way to concatenate 1000 strings in Java?
questions.explanation: StringBuilder is mutable and avoids creating new String objects per concatenation. The + operator creates a new String object each time.

questions.text: What will happen? Integer a = 128; Integer b = 128; System.out.println(a == b);
questions.explanation: Java caches Integer values from -128 to 127. For 128, new objects are created, so == compares references → false.

questions.text: In Amazon's Leadership Principles, 'Customer Obsession' means:
options: Leaders start with the customer and work backwards
questions.explanation: Amazon's Customer Obsession principle: Leaders start with the customer and work backwards to develop solutions.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a circuit breaker pattern in microservices?
options: To prevent cascading failures by stopping calls to a failing service
questions.explanation: Circuit breaker monitors failures and stops requests to a failing service, allowing it to recover and preventing system-wide failure.

questions.text: What is eventual consistency in distributed systems?
options: Given enough time, all nodes will have the same data
Only one node has correct data
questions.explanation: Eventual consistency guarantees that all replicas will converge to the same value eventually, though they may temporarily differ.

questions.text: Which data structure would you use to find the k-th largest element efficiently?
questions.explanation: A min-heap of size k maintains the k largest elements. The root (min of the heap) is the k-th largest.

questions.text: If all efficient systems are scalable, and some scalable systems are fault-tolerant, then:
options: Some efficient systems may be fault-tolerant
questions.explanation: All efficient→scalable. Some scalable→fault-tolerant. Therefore some efficient systems might be fault-tolerant (possibility, not certainty).

questions.text: A project manager must decide between 3 approaches. Each takes 2, 4, or 8 weeks. If approach 1 fails (40% chance), try approach 2. If approach 2 fails (30% chance), try approach 3. Expected minimum time if all could be parallel:
questions.explanation: If all three can run in parallel, the minimum time needed is 2 weeks (shortest approach).

questions.text: A team of 5 needs to go from floor 1 to floor 20. Elevator holds 3. Minimum elevator trips needed:
questions.explanation: Trip 1: 3 people go up. Trip 2: remaining 2 go up. Minimum = 2 trips.

questions.text: You have 8 identical-looking balls. One is heavier. Minimum weighings to find it using a balance scale:
questions.explanation: Divide into 3 groups: 3+3+2. Weigh 3 vs 3: if equal, heavy ball is in the 2 (1 more weighing). If unequal, weigh 1 vs 1 from heavier group. Max 2 weighings.

questions.text: A function takes O(n log n). For n=1000, it takes 1 second. For n=1,000,000, approximately:
questions.explanation: Ratio = (10⁶ × log 10⁶)/(10³ × log 10³) = 1000 × (20/10) = 2000. Approx 2000 seconds.

questions.text: 5 friends each shake hands exactly once with every other friend. Total handshakes:
questions.explanation: C(5,2) = 10 handshakes.

questions.text: In a meeting, 3 managers each report to all other managers. No self-loops. Total ordered reporting pairs:
questions.explanation: Ordered pairs among 3: 3×2=6 (A→B, A→C, B→A, B→C, C→A, C→B).

questions.text: A server handles 100 req/sec. If request rate doubles and server speed stays same, queue grows by:
questions.explanation: Server handles 100, incoming=200. Queue grows at 200-100=100 req/sec.

questions.text: If A implies B, and B implies C, and C is false, then:
options: A is false, B is false
A is true, B is false
A is false, B is true
questions.explanation: C is false → B is false (contrapositive of B→C) → A is false (contrapositive of A→B).

questions.text: You need to design a system for 1 million users. Which is the biggest bottleneck?
questions.explanation: A single un-indexed database is the biggest bottleneck for scale — all queries would be slow full table scans.

questions.text: A binary number 1010 in decimal is:
What is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height 4?
questions.explanation: Maximum nodes = 2^(h+1) - 1 = 2^5 - 1 = 31 (where height 4 means 5 levels, 0 to 4).
